title: Corner C3 - Walking Sprite Sheets Spec
summary: 4-directional walking animations for all agents. 6 frames per direction. Consistent with existing idle/thinking/speaking/done sprites.
content:
Corner C3: Walking Sprite Sheets Spec

Steffen | 2026-03-16 For Bobby + sprite generation. Walking is the north star animation. These are the frame specs for Gemini to generate.

Isometric Directions

In isometric space, there are 4 meaningful walking directions:

Direction Compass Screen Motion Description
NE North-East Up-right Walking toward top-right of screen
NW North-West Up-left Walking toward top-left of screen
SE South-East Down-right Walking toward bottom-right (toward camera)
SW South-West Down-left Walking toward bottom-left (toward camera)

SE is the default facing direction (toward camera). Most walking will be NE/SW (along the main corridors of the L-shaped building).

Frame Spec (Per Direction, Per Agent)

Each walking direction has 6 frames of animation.

Walk Cycle Breakdown

Frame Duration Description
1 150ms Contact: Right foot forward, arms at opposite swing. Weight shifting.
2 150ms Passing: Left foot passing right, body centered. Slight rise (1px up).
3 150ms Contact: Left foot forward, arms swapped. Weight on left.
4 150ms Passing: Right foot passing left, body centered. 1px up again.
5 150ms Same as frame 1 but with slight forward lean (1px). Full stride.
6 150ms Same as frame 2. Completes one full walk cycle.

Total cycle duration: 900ms (6 frames x 150ms) Walk speed: 1 tile (64px grid) per 900ms. Approximately 1 room width per second.

The 1px Bounce

Frames 2 and 4 have the character 1px higher than frames 1, 3, 5, 6. This creates the natural walking bounce that makes pixel art feel alive. Without it, the character slides like an ice skater.

Arm Swing

Standard opposite-arm swing:

  • Frame 1, 5: Right foot forward, left arm forward, right arm back
  • Frame 3: Left foot forward, right arm forward, left arm back
  • Frame 2, 4, 6: Arms at neutral (passing through)

Arms are only 1-2px elements at 32px sprite size, so the swing is subtle. At 64px (room detail zoom), it becomes more visible.

Direction-Specific Notes

SE (Toward Camera, Primary Direction)

  • Agent faces down-right
  • Full face visible (both eyes, if the sprite has them)
  • Most detailed direction (this is what you see most)
  • Feet move: right foot goes down-right, left foot goes down-left

NW (Away from Camera)

  • Agent faces up-left
  • Back of head visible, no face
  • Less detail needed (it's the back view)
  • Mirror of SE with back turned

NE (Top-Right)

  • Agent faces up-right
  • Right side of face visible
  • Body angled, one arm more visible than the other

SW (Bottom-Left)

  • Agent faces down-left
  • Left side of face visible
  • Mirror of NE but facing the other way

Per-Agent Walking Personality

Walking should feel different per agent, even within the same 6-frame structure.

Agent Walk Style Notes
Patrik Confident stride Upright posture, slightly wider steps. Boss walk.
Mom Purposeful, slightly fast Leans forward, tablet in hand. Going somewhere important.
Alex Measured, scholarly Hands may be behind back. Slow, deliberate steps.
Steve Precise, efficient Minimal arm swing. Straight path. No wasted movement.
Steffen Relaxed, creative Slight lean, one hand in pocket or holding something (pen). Easy sway.
Bobby Slouched, hoodie shuffle Headphones on, slight forward lean. Developer walk. Steps are closer together.
Colton Upright, methodical Similar to Steve but slightly faster. Carrying a document.
Cleo Energetic, bouncy More pronounced 1px bounce. Headphones bouncing.
Tony Casual swagger Phone in hand, slight side-to-side sway. Trendy walk.
Jacob Business hustle Fast-looking walk. Headset on, notepad under arm. Grinding energy.
Elmo Careful, clinical Small steps. Lab coat swishes slightly. Precise.
Elon Utilitarian Fastest walk speed. No personality embellishment. Point A to point B.
Pixel Light, quick Smallest sprite. Quick little steps. Tech-forward energy.

Door Transition Frames

When a character reaches a doorway:

Entering (2 frames, 200ms total)

Frame Duration Description
Enter-1 100ms Character at door threshold. Feet at the door line.
Enter-2 100ms Character steps through. Brief opacity dip to 70% as they pass through the wall thickness (2-4px). Then back to 100%.

Exiting (2 frames, 200ms total)

Same as entering but in reverse. The character appears at the door of the new room and takes a step in.

Open Walls (Main Hall connections)

No door transition needed. Characters walk straight through. No opacity dip.

Spritesheet Format

File Naming

sprites/
  {agent}/
    walk-ne.png  (6 frames, horizontal strip)
    walk-nw.png  (6 frames)
    walk-se.png  (6 frames)
    walk-sw.png  (6 frames)

Or a single sheet per agent:

sprites/
  {agent}-walk.png  (4 rows x 6 cols = 24 frames)

Row order: NE, NW, SE, SW (top to bottom)

Dimensions

  • Per frame: 32x32px (standard), 64x64px (detail)
  • Strip (6 frames): 192x32px (standard), 384x64px (detail)
  • Full sheet (4 directions x 6 frames): 192x128px (standard), 384x256px (detail)

Rendering Rules

  • Transparent background (PNG-32)
  • No anti-aliasing (hard pixel edges)
  • 1px black outline (#1A1A2E) on all characters
  • Same color palette as the existing idle/thinking/speaking/done sprites
  • agentColor as the dominant accent

Pathfinding (for Bobby)

Algorithm

Use the adjacency map from gridSpec.js. Simple BFS (breadth-first search) is sufficient for 14 rooms.

Walk Triggers

Trigger From To Behavior
Handoff Sender's desk Receiver's room door Walk to deliver, leave note, walk back
Meeting Visiting agent's desk Host's room (near door) Walk to room, stay for duration, walk back
Bathroom (death) Agent's desk Nearest exterior door Walk to exit, disappear
Return (recovery) Nearest exterior door Agent's desk Enter, walk to desk, sit

Walk Queue

  • Only one agent walks at a time (prevents visual chaos)
  • Queue walks with 500ms delay between starts
  • Priority: death/recovery > handoff > meeting

Path Visualization (Debug)

For development: render the walk path as a faint dotted line (1px, agentColor at 10%). Hidden in production.

C3 MVP vs C3.1

C3 MVP (Bobby builds this)

  • Walking sprites: use the idle sprite sliding along the path (translateX/Y animation)
  • No per-frame walk animation (just the character moving)
  • This still looks decent because the room dimming + door transitions sell the movement
  • Walk speed: same (1 tile/900ms)

C3.1 (After sprites are generated)

  • Replace the sliding idle sprite with the full 6-frame walk cycle
  • 4 directional sprites based on movement direction
  • Door transition opacity dips
  • Per-agent walk personality

The C3 MVP approach lets Bobby build the pathfinding and walk trigger logic without waiting for sprite generation. The visual upgrade is a drop-in replacement.

Generation Prompt for Gemini

When generating walk sprites, use this prompt structure:

Isometric pixel art walk cycle for [agent name], 32x32px, [direction] facing.
6 frames in a horizontal strip on transparent background.
Character: [description from c2-sprite-spec.md silhouette section].
Accent color: [agentColor hex].
Walk style: [personality from table above].
Standard walk cycle: contact-passing-contact-passing-contact-passing.
1px bounce on frames 2 and 4.
1px black outline on character.
Warm, slightly saturated colors.
2:1 isometric ratio.
No anti-aliasing.

Run 4 prompts per agent (one per direction). Total: 13 agents x 4 directions = 52 sprite sheets. Or 13 full walk sheets at 4 rows each.

Walking is what makes Corner feel alive. The isometric office goes from a static diorama to a living world. Bobby builds the pathfinding in Step 9. Sprites generate when ready.
